preamble: Voicing of the voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕ] to its voiced counterpart [dʑ] keeps the place and manner of articulation and adds vocal-fold vibration, typically in a voiced environment. Korean voices /tɕ/ (ㅈ) to [dʑ] allophonically between sonorants, and Japanese rendaku voices the initial ち [tɕi] of the second member of a compound to ぢ [dʑi] (intervocalically often realized as the fricative [ʑi]).

examples.note: The lax stops and affricate /p, t, tɕ, k/ are voiced [b, d, dʑ, ɡ] between sonorants and voiceless elsewhere; this is allophonic.
Rendaku (sequential voicing) voices the initial consonant of the second compound member; the voiced affricate is often lenited to [ʑ] between vowels, and Wiktionary transcribes this word [ha̠na̠ʑi].

sources: Vance, T. J. (2015). Rendaku. In H. Kubozono (Ed.), Handbook of Japanese Phonetics and Phonology. De Gruyter Mouton.
